thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 tail latency and streaming stalls detected for eu-west2 egress path. Metric spike started ~3322109980. Affected service: streaming-gateway (route: /v1/streams). Auto-runbook triggered: vpc-egress-triage. Paging oncall: @sandeep

ana: saw the pager. I'm on audio. Quick ask: is this primarily TLS handshake spikes, or are we seeing DNS/NAT issues too?

sandeep (oncall): initial check: p95 up ~150ms -> 310ms, p99 from 420ms -> 1.6s. Streaming tail (last-token) stalls and some client resends. Net graphs show increased SYN-ACK RTTs and TLS handshake retransmits in cross-zone flows.

lina: adding logs from the internal probe hitting eu-west2 frontends:
```
$ curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}\n" -s -o /dev/null https://internal-probe.eu-west2.local/health
0.342 1.682
```
connect ~342ms, time to first byte ~1.68s. Also seeing lots of truncated DNS responses and retries from the gateways:
`resolver_count=3 failures=87/5m`

marc: netops telemetry shows NAT ephemeral port exhaustion on a subset of AZs (az-b, az-c). Connection reuse pattern changed after a deploy earlier today that increased upstream fanout. NAT metrics: ephemeral_ports_used ~ 98%, conntrack high.

netops: confirmed. NAT gateway logs: `EPEMPTY` surges on 10.0.2.x pool. We also see crosszone route flaps; BGP adjacency stable but internal route churn causing occasional hairpin.

ana: OK — priority mitigation options? We need fast, low-risk steps: 1) reduce new ephemeral port pressure; 2) reroute traffic away from impacted AZs; 3) prevent client retries from amplifying load.

sandeep (oncall): executing steps in order. Step 1: enable NAT port pooling expansion for eu-west2 for affected node pool. Command (internal infra API):
```
# increase ephemeral ports from 16k->32k for nat-pool-eu-west2-1
POST /infra/v1/nat/pools/nat-pool-eu-west2-1/scale {"max_ports": 32768}
```
I pushed the request, infra accepted. Watching metrics.

lina: Step 2: apply smart-routing override to prefer eu-west3 and eu-north1 for streaming endpoints for 10m window. Patch to routing policy: `route-policy: prefer-region(eu-west3,eu-north1) for service streaming-gateway if region==eu-west2`.

marc: Applying routing override now. This will shift ~35% of traffic during the window. Note: we may see brief increase in latency for those flows as they cross regions but shouldn't be as bad as current tail.

incident-bot: Runbook note: if NAT expansion + reroute not effective in 10m, escalate to Tier2 network (netops) and consider spinning temporary dedicated egress instances in eu-west2 to absorb connections.

netops: also opening NAT gateway failover to secondary egress IP pool for az-b. This is low-risk. Doing a staged rotation to avoid flapping.

ana: also reducing client retry budget via config to avoid thundering herd: set `client_retry_policy.max_retries=1` for streaming route. Patch queued.

sandeep (oncall): status update ~5m after mitigations: ephemeral_ports_used -> 72%, p95 -> 180ms, p99 -> 420ms, streaming stalls decreased but still present for a small % of connections. Good partial improvement.

lina: DNS error rate dropped after reroute (we moved away from overloaded resolver mesh). TLS handshake retransmits also down 60%.

marc: netops still seeing intermittent packet loss on crosszone link between az-b and az-c during the window; chasing queuebacklog on one router. Raising severity and bringing in netops lead @eva.

eva: on it. I'm running per-hop captures and will coordinate link-level mitigation (queue tuning and micro-burst shaping). ETA 12m.

incident-bot: Paging escalation to netops (priority high).

ana: customer impact: initial surge impacted ~0.7% of streaming sessions resulting in visible stalls or reconnects. Highlighted customers: 2 enterprise customers reported degraded voice/video stitching in EU regions. Support notified and a workaround (reconnect) suggested.

sandeep (oncall): will run post-mortem checklist: collect pcap, NAT logs, resolver logs, routing change events, and the deploy diff from earlier today. Tagged this incident as P1 until full recovery confirmed.

netops: after applying queue shaping and rotating the failing router, packetloss -> near 0. Flow metrics steady.

marc: confirm: p99 now ~220-290ms and streaming tail stalls at baseline. NAT ports stable. Rolling back routing override to normal gradually over 10m to avoid re-exposing the impact.

lina: rolling back client retry cap as well.

ana: good. I'll draft the customer-facing summary for support and sla impacts. Key facts: timeline, root cause hypothesis (NAT ephemeral exhaustion + cross-zone queueing causing TLS handshake spikes and DNS retries), mitigations (NAT pool expansion, routing override, router queue shaping), and customer mitigation steps.

eva: adding network remediation notes to runbook: increase default nat pool for eu regions, add early-warning alert for ephemeral_ports > 85%, and add a play to automatically prefer local resolvers during surges.

sandeep (oncall): handing off to marc/netops for follow-up and postmortem. Next oncall: @eva will monitor for 1hr and confirm clean. I'm marking the incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: mitigation confirmed at 3322110360. Postmortem assigned: owners=[netops, infra, deploy-team]. Runbook updated: vpc-egress-triage.

ana: thanks everyone. I'll file a short postmortem and include mitigation timelines and performance graphs. :thumbsup:

marc: adding a note to the deployment team to review the earlier fanout change. Might need a gradual rollout and capacity testing.

netops: collecting final artifacts and will upload to the incident tracker.

eva: monitoring OK for now, will keep an eye for 60m and then close.

sandeep (oncall): great job all.
